spec.title: Migration from single-writer WAL and redbook composition

facts.INCOMPAT-WAL: `wal@1` requires one shared repository `WAL.xml` plus root `CONTINUE.md` to own personal session continuity. It is an alternative storage/authority model and must not own the same personal context concurrently with this flow. This is not a global prohibition on installing both packages for separately scoped use.
facts.INCOMPAT-WAL-SPECSPACES: `wal-specspaces@1` multiplies that model by project root, not by contributor, branch or central session. It therefore remains single-writer within each specspace and must not compete with this flow for the same context. Separate explicit scopes may select different continuity owners.
facts.COMPAT-CAMPAIGN: `campaign-plans@1` is compatible when a repository campaign plan is a deliberately shared, integrator-owned contract. Its plan/ledger must not replace contributors' local adaptive plans, and non-integrators submit uniquely named records.
facts.COMPAT-MODES: `operating-modes@1` remains a session-scoped codeword system. Persistent interaction/planning settings in this flow are user preferences, not codewords and not permission to cross red lines.
facts.COMPAT-OTHER-REDBOOK: The remaining redbook@1 laws are compatible. Where an older document says “two writers” or puts WAL last in an authority chain, read “two or more writers” and “volatile local/shared projection” respectively; this flow supplies the N-writer coordination layer.

p.EDITION-LAW: The owner may change the tested roster of any Redbook version. Before an agent overwrites an existing version's composition, offer a new version as an alternative unless the owner has already explicitly chosen. The current prototype composition work stays 1.0.0 by owner decision. Continuity alternatives are exclusive within the Redbook selection group, not globally incompatible package names. Effective selection and content must remain explicit and inspectable; this flow does not implement or pretend to ship the planned variant resolver.

p.TUNING-NOW: With the current resolver, per-edge deep `exclude` remains an available consumer-side tuning mechanism. Exclusion narrows only the named dependency subtree and remains visible in the root manifest and lock/effective set.

p.DIRECT-EDGES: Remove any direct root edges to `wal` and `wal-specspaces` for the context being migrated; an exclusion on the redbook edge cannot cancel an independent root path. After `vibe install --offline`, inspect `vibe.lock`, the effective package tree and generated boot lane: neither competing legacy continuity instruction may govern that context. Separately scoped package use is not prohibited.

facts.MIGRATE-INVENTORY: Inventory current `WAL.xml`, `CONTINUE.md`, root mode/planning files, specspace state, campaign plans, branch/worktree state and any unique reports. Do not delete first.
facts.MIGRATE-LOCAL: Create the matching `~/.vibe/steward` context. Preserve explicit owner settings (for example a root `mode = "auto"`) as context settings, construct the complete local plan, and mark unverified work candidate.
facts.MIGRATE-PROMOTE: Promote stable project facts and decisions out of volatile legacy files into their governing repository homes. Keep a shared campaign contract only when an integrator is named.
facts.MIGRATE-BOOT: Change manifest composition, regenerate offline, and replace repo boot text that mandates a personal WAL with the short multi-user-planning signpost. Keep harness entry files byte-identical when the project requires mirrors.
facts.MIGRATE-CONTINUATION: Prove the new state with a fresh owner-facing central session that resolves the binding and finds the full route, accepted boundary and every candidate from settings, complete plan and repository evidence without chat history or session, handoff, receipt or takeover documents. A separate explicit offer/receipt dogfood is optional unless the owner requests formal handoff.
facts.MIGRATE-HANDOFF: Retired v0.2 migration gate. Its successor is `MIGRATE-CONTINUATION`; formal handoff dogfood is optional unless explicitly requested.
facts.MIGRATE-RETIRE: Only after project-fact promotion and successful fresh casual continuation may legacy personal state be removed or archived. Cleanup is its own reviewed change.

p.SPECSPACE-TOPOLOGY: A repository may retain `SPECSPACES.md` as stable topology: name, root and boot contract. Remove personal defaults, current status and mutable session continuation from the shared registry. Each contributor's exact target/default and plan live in a local context.

p.TARGET-RESOLUTION: Resolve target by: explicit owner name or directory; unambiguous task/cwd inside a registered root; current local context; otherwise host project. Explicit always wins, unknown names are surfaced, and one session has one focus unless it announces a cross-project task.

p.BOOT-SCOPING: A targeted specspace session reads host-wide commit/safety rules plus the target's own boot and relevant specs; it does not load unrelated host/specspace plans. Continuity comes from the target-bound user-local context, not a specspace WAL.

p.MIXED-MODE-REFUSAL: If generated boot activates this flow and `wal` or `wal-specspaces` as competing continuity owners for the same context, do not choose whichever text appears later. Stop affected central state mutation, report the conflict and repair composition or explicit scope. Mere package presence, data/reference use or a separately scoped context does not establish competing authority.
